precepts.text: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.
precepts.point: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap. When you put in the sin, the consequences are going to happen. For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption: you will be judged by it. But he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting: when you sow yourself into the scriptures, the Lord gives blessings, favor, mercy, and abundance.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
The Lord set both harvests before Israel from the beginning: “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.”

What you put in, you are going to get; you are going to receive a reward. Life and blessing for the one who sows to the Spirit, death and cursing for the one who sows to his flesh. Heaven and earth are called as witnesses, so no one can say he was not told. God is not mocked.

And the choice reaches past you: choose life “that both thou and thy seed may live.” What a man sows, his children reap with him.

precepts.text: I call heaven and earth to record: life and death, blessing and cursing, are set before you, so choose life; everything is being recorded, every idle word.
precepts.point: The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions: keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes, and commandments and have life.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live”. Everything is being recorded, every idle word.

Baal-peor showed both sides of it: “all the men that followed Baal–peor, the Lord thy God hath destroyed them”, and “ye that did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day.” Death for those who followed that foolishness, life for those who cleaved to him.

The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions. Keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes and commandments and have life. Life and death are set before you, so choose life.

precepts.text: Calling the blessing and the curse to mind is Israel remembering themselves in the land of their captivities.
precepts.point: And shalt return unto the Lord thy God, and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee, thou and thy children, with all thine heart and with all thy soul. The stipulation of returning is keeping the commandments; you cannot just say I accept the Lord in my heart. That does not work. And your children must be in order under your household too; they cannot fake it either.

note.label: Deuteronomy 30: Call the Curses to Mind and Choose Life

precepts.why:
With all that being said in the curses, here is the goodness of the Most High: he said, I am going to punish you, but he gave us the solution to get up out of the curses. “when all these things are come upon thee, the blessing and the curse, which I have set before thee, and thou shalt call them to mind among all the nations, whither the Lord thy God hath driven thee”. Baruch tells you what calling them to mind is: “For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.”

The Most High knew we would not hear him, stiffnecked as we are, so the remembering happens in the land of our captivities. We are remembering ourselves now: we know we got here on ships, we know we did not speak the white man's language when he came to the west coast of Africa, we know we rise when the alarm clock goes off and work for food, water and drink, and we know Christianity is a slave religion forced on our ancestors. That is calling the curses to mind.

Then the stipulation: “And shalt return unto the Lord thy God, and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day, thou and thy children, with all thine heart, and with all thy soul”. Returning is keeping the commandments. You cannot just say I accept the Lord in my heart; that does not work. And your children must be in order under your household too; they cannot fake it either.

precepts.text: He shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds; Christ gathers Israel, nobody else.
precepts.point: If any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven, from thence will he fetch thee: no matter where we are in the four corners of the earth, if we repent and endure to the end, Christ said, I am coming to get you.

note.label: Deuteronomy 30: Call the Curses to Mind and Choose Life

precepts.why:
“That then the Lord thy God will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations, whither the Lord thy God hath scattered thee.” It did not say the League of Nations, NATO or an airline jet will gather us. Christ says who: “And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Christ gathers Israel, nobody else.

The Most High is sending Christ to come and get us and take us back to the land, the same way he delivered us out of Egypt himself, with the angel leading, and no Amorite, Greek or Roman helping. There is nothing new under the sun. That is how we know the people over in the land now are not the people of the book: Israel returns by the hand of the Most High, not by planes.

“If any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven, from thence will the Lord thy God gather thee, and from thence will he fetch thee”: from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other. No matter where we are in the four corners of the earth, if we repent and endure to the end, Christ said, I am coming to get you.

precepts.text: Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye; that is the life the Most High tells you to choose.
precepts.point: He already told you what is up. The life he is telling you to choose is in Proverbs: keep my commandments and live. The commandments give you life; they are your spiritual force field out on the streets in the land of wickedness.

note.label: Deuteronomy 30: Call the Curses to Mind and Choose Life

precepts.why:
Highlight verse 19 if you do not have it highlighted: “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live”. He already told you what is up: the blessing, the curse, and the way back. Now he says choose.

What is the life he tells you to choose? Solomon says it: “Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” The commandments give you life. They are your spiritual force field out on the streets in the land of wickedness. To choose life is to keep the commandments and hold the law as the apple of thine eye, and that is how both thou and thy seed may live.

precepts.text: His angels that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word; obeying his voice is keeping his commandments.
precepts.point: What is his voice again? Precept upon precept: the voice of the Lord is his commandments, so cleave unto him by doing them, that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

note.label: Deuteronomy 30: Call the Curses to Mind and Choose Life

precepts.why:
“That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days”. What is his voice again? Precept upon precept: “Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.” The angels hearken unto his voice by doing his commandments. The voice of the Lord is his commandments.

So obeying his voice is keeping his commandments, and you cleave unto him by doing them. He is thy life and the length of thy days, “that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.”

precepts.text: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.
precepts.point: There was not a word of all that Moses commanded which Joshua read not before all the congregation, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them: those were the strangers that fell in line with Israel, with the fear of the Lord in them, as Rahab had.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why:
Joshua read “the blessings and cursings, according to all that is written in the book of the law.” Moses set them before the people this way: “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live”.

Heaven and earth are called to record: everything we do is recorded. Life and death, blessing and cursing, are set before us. We tell our neighbor God bless you, but by the same book the Most High and Christ will curse you too if you do not keep the laws. It is the one thing left optional, so choose life, for it is not just you that pays but thy seed as well.

precepts.text: I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing; therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live, that thou mayest love the Lord thy God, obey his voice, and cleave unto him.
precepts.point: Moses said the same thing: he set life and death, blessing and cursing before Israel and said choose life. Deuteronomy 28 laid it out, blessings in verses 1 through 14 if Israel obeyed, to be above all people and rule; curses from 15 down to 68 if not. Israel chose the cursing and the death, and that is what we are in now, trying to come back and get out of it.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

precepts.why:
“choose you this day whom ye will serve”. Moses said the same thing: “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days”.

Deuteronomy 28 laid it out: blessings in verses 1 through 14 if Israel obeyed, to be above all people and rule; curses from 15 down to 68 if not. Israel chose the cursing and the death, and that is what we are in now, trying to come back and get out of it.

A lot of people hang “as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord” up in the house and do not keep one law; everybody reads this verse and reads nothing before it about being put to death for going off. Choosing life means loving the Lord, obeying his voice and cleaving unto him. Lord willing they have space and time to repent.

precepts.text: When the blessing and the curse are come upon them and they return to the Most High among the nations, he promises to gather them from all the peoples where he scattered them, even from the outmost parts of heaven, the very promise Nehemiah pleads.
precepts.point: This is Nehemiah quoting Deuteronomy 28, holding the Most High to what Moses had already taught in the wilderness, both the scattering and the gathering.

note.label: Nehemiah 1: Nehemiah's Prayer for Jerusalem

precepts.why:
Nehemiah confesses that Israel “have not kept the commandments, nor the statutes, nor the judgments, which thou commandedst thy servant Moses”, and then pleads the word the Most High gave Moses: “If ye transgress, I will scatter you abroad among the nations: But if ye turn unto me, and keep my commandments, and do them; though there were of you cast out unto the uttermost part of the heaven, yet will I gather them from thence”.

This is that promise. Moses said that when “the blessing and the curse” have come upon them and they “call them to mind among all the nations, whither the Lord thy God hath driven thee, And shalt return unto the Lord thy God, and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day”, then “the Lord thy God will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations, whither the Lord thy God hath scattered thee. If any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven, from thence will the Lord thy God gather thee”.

Nehemiah is holding the Most High to what Moses had already taught in the wilderness, both the scattering and the gathering. The curse for transgressing is scattering among the nations; the promise for turning and keeping the commandments is gathering from the outmost parts of heaven to the place he has chosen to set his name. Nehemiah's prayer rests on that word.

precepts.text: The Most High will put all these curses upon our enemies and on them that hate and persecute us.
precepts.point: Jeremiah prayed for the Most High's curse on the enemy because he knew the heathen would have to go through the curses of Deuteronomy 28 when it is all said and done; we are the ones redeemed from the curse, and we will see our enemies go through it for eternity while we reign forever.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

precepts.why:
Jeremiah prays, “Render unto them a recompence, O Lord, according to the work of their hands. Give them sorrow of heart, thy curse unto them.” He prayed for the Most High's curse on the enemy because he knew what was written: “And the Lord thy God will put all these curses upon thine enemies, and on them that hate thee, which persecuted thee.”

The heathen will have to go through the curses of Deuteronomy 28 when it is all said and done. The Most High will put all these curses upon our enemies and on them that hate and persecute us; that is the recompence according to the work of their hands, and Jeremiah asked for it out of the low dungeon.
